title: How Zerodha Makes Money With ₹0 Brokerage
description:
Zerodha, one of India's biggest stockbrokers, charges ₹0 brokerage when you buy shares to hold, yet it earned about ₹4,283 crore (about ₹43 billion) in net profit in the year to March 2026. The money comes from traders, who pay up to ₹20 per intraday, futures or options order (brokerage of about ₹2,738 crore), from interest income (about ₹2,269 crore) and from margin loans (about 10% of revenue). SEBI found 87.7% of individual futures and options traders lost money in FY2025-26.

Sources: Zerodha, '16 years of Zerodha: Fresh enthusiasm' (Nithin Kamath, 26 Aug 2026), FY2025-26 figures as reported by Inc42 (26-28 Aug 2026) and IANS (27 Aug 2026); Zerodha charges page (checked 22 Nov 2026); SEBI, 'Profitability of Individual Traders in the Equity Derivatives Segment (FY25-FY26)' (Aug 2026). 1 crore = 10 million. Not financial advice.

scenes.say: Zerodha, one of India's biggest stockbrokers, charges nothing when you buy shares to keep. Yet in its latest financial year, it made about forty-three billion rupees in profit.

visual.label: Zerodha's profit, year to March 2026
visual.sub: ₹4,283 crore · ₹0 brokerage to buy and hold

scenes.say: The trick? Investors who buy and hold pay zero. Traders pay. Every intraday, futures or options order costs up to twenty rupees.
That brokerage brought in about twenty-seven billion rupees. Almost as big: interest income, about twenty-three billion.
It also lends traders money to buy shares. These margin loans are now about a tenth of its revenue.
The catch: India's market regulator found that in the same year, nearly nine in ten individual futures and options traders lost money.

visual.label: of individual F&O traders lost money

scenes.say: So investing really can be free. The bill is paid by people who trade a lot.
